adrianne.yoga · for Daegan, from Jimmy & Claude · round 2

Three homepages for Adrianne

Same approved words, three completely different designs. Each one was built from deep research (20 top yoga sites, 43 real student reviews, her public bios, her own tagline and butterfly), checked at phone, tablet and desktop size, scored by a fresh critic next to The Class, Molly Baz and Patrick Beach, and fixed. Open them on your phone first. That's where her students will land after class.

"Open" shows the clean client view. "Open with review marks" shows every suggested line and every fact still to confirm, so you can keep or cut each one. Photo spots are designed placeholders until her real photos arrive. Forms are demos and don't send anything yet.

Critic's #1 · the gift

A · After Class

The note card is the hero. When a student sends a note, the card folds, flies onto her wall and gets a cat stamp: "Read aloud tonight." It also has the class picker ("Take a class for your first time"), her week across every studio, and one door at a time for studios, companies and schools.

Open AOpen with review marks
Critic's #2 · the utility

B · This Week with Adrianne

Students follow teachers, not studios. Their first question is "where is she this week?" This one answers it on the first screen: a bold cobalt and sunshine class board that knows today's date, filters by neighborhood, and has the best single feature of the round, "Take a class for [your first time ▾]".

Open BOpen with review marks
Critic's #3 · the calm

C · One Breath

The last 30 seconds of savasana, then the lights come up. A large disc breathes behind the question (in for 4, out for 6), "Take one breath. Then tell me." guides one breath into the note, and her butterfly travels down her story.

Open COpen with review marks

Our recommendation: lead with A

A is the one that makes a student smile and makes Adrianne feel loved. Every note becomes a little ceremony. B's picker and C's breath are already folded into A, so you can pick A and still keep the best of the other two. Or mix: "A, in B's colors" is a fine answer.

What lifts any of them past every yoga site out there: 15–30 real photos of her teaching, plus the cats. Then we wire the note wall, set up the weekly class list she can update in two minutes, and launch on adrianne.yoga.
